label: BMW S70/2 6.1 L V12 (McLaren F1)

sources.what: McLaren Automotive specification sheet 'McLaren F1 GT Roadcar', powertrain type S 70/2 (third-party host). Manufacturer; the GT uses the standard road-car engine.
English Wikipedia McLaren F1 page; rev limit, injection, catalysts.
English Wikipedia BMW M70 page, S70/2 section and version table.

notes: Sourced: bore, stroke, compression, 60-degree V12, four valves per cylinder, twelve individual throttles, 7500 rpm limit. The firing order is ASSUMED: none is published for the S70/2, nor its crank layout. A conventional even-firing 60-degree V12 is used (six shared pins 120 degrees apart, firing every 60 degrees) with the order 1-7-5-11-3-9-6-12-2-8-4-10, cylinders 1-6 on one bank, which is the order one source gives for the related two-valve BMW M70. Estimated, not sourced: rod length, valve diameters and lifts, cam timing and duration (variable inlet timing on the real engine; one fixed timing is used), intake trumpet length and diameter, the whole exhaust layout (four 3-into-1 manifolds into one cross-over, two outlets) and its sizes, idle speed. The carbon airbox the real throttles breathe from is not modelled: individual throttles open to the air here. Left to the simulator's defaults: collector volume, muffler, flywheel inertia. Also estimates: friction_scale, heat_q, burn_scale (the simulator's friction, heat-release and burn-rate scales), set with the other estimated fields so that simulated torque and power come near the published figures; no sourced number was changed.

vehicle.name: McLaren F1 (1994)
vehicle.notes: Six-speed manual. Curb weight, gear ratios, tyre and top speed from McLaren's specification sheet. Final drive 2.93 is OUR effective figure: McLaren's published 2.37 does not reproduce its own road speed per 1,000 rpm in any gear (it is about 1.24 times too tall, so a further reduction appears to be unpublished); 2.93 is solved from the sheet's mph per 1,000 rpm and the estimated rolling radius, and fits every gear within 2%. The 386 km/h top speed is the 1998 record run with the rev limit raised to 8,300 rpm; at the standard 7,500 rpm limit the car is geared for about 360 km/h. Estimated: rolling radius from the tyre size.
